### ram-az-names-differ-use-az-ids

**Claim.** AWS maps physical Availability Zones randomly to AZ names for each account, so us-east-1a in one account may be a different location in another; an AZ ID such as use1-az1 is the same physical location in every account, and a shared subnet is available in the consumer's AZ with the same AZ ID.

**Write it as.** `maps the physical Availability Zones randomly` · `the same physical location in every AWS account` · `whose AZ ID is also use1-az2`

**Scope.** subnets shared across accounts.

> "AWS maps the physical Availability Zones randomly to the Availability Zone names for each AWS account."
> — [Availability Zone IDs for your AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/working-with-az-ids.html)

> "For example, use1-az1 is an AZ ID for an Availability Zone in the us-east-1 Region and it represents the same physical location in every AWS account."
> — [Availability Zone IDs for your AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/working-with-az-ids.html)

> "For example, if you share a subnet in the Availability Zone with the AZ ID use1-az2 with another account, this subnet is available to that account in the Availability Zone whose AZ ID is also use1-az2."
> — [Availability Zone IDs for your AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/working-with-az-ids.html)

### ram-cannot-add-outside-org-or-ous

**Scope.** RAM resource share principals.

### ram-share-by-account-id-any-account

**Claim.** With RAM you can share with all accounts in the organization or only with accounts in specified OUs, and you can also share with specific AWS accounts by account ID whether or not they are in an organization.

**Write it as.** `share resources with all the other accounts` · `share with specific AWS accounts by account ID` · `whether the account is part of an organization`

**Scope.** AWS RAM principals; resource type must allow sharing outside the organization.

> "If your account is managed by AWS Organizations, you can share resources with all the other accounts in the organization or only those accounts contained by one or more specified organizational units (OUs). You can also share with specific AWS accounts by account ID, regardless of whether the account is part of an organization."
> — [What is AWS Resource Access Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/what-is.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

You can share only subnets you create yourself. | No | No <br />Can share with **only** AWS accounts in its own organization. | No | No" (columns: Resource type and code | Use case | Can share with IAM users and roles | Can share with accounts outside its organization | Can use customer managed permissions | Can share with service principals)

### ram-tgw-shared-attachment-accept

**Claim.** An invited account must accept the transit gateway resource share in RAM before it can use the transit gateway, and if Auto accept shared attachments was not enabled when the transit gateway was created, cross-account (shared) attachments must be accepted manually.

**Write it as.** `You must accept the resource share` · `you must manually accept cross-account (shared) attachment` · `Auto accept shared attachments`

**Scope.** transit gateway shared through RAM; Auto accept shared attachments not enabled.

> "If you were added to a resource share, you receive an invitation to join the resource share. You must accept the resource share through the AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) console before you can access the shared resources."
> — [Accept an AWS Transit Gateway resource share using the AWS Resource Access Manager console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/share-accept-tgw.html)

> "If you didn't enable the Auto accept shared attachments functionality when you created your transit gateway, you must manually accept cross-account (shared) attachment using either the Amazon VPC Console or the AWS CLI."
> — [Accept a shared attachment in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/acccept-tgw-attach.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### ram-vpc-participant-resources-count-participant-quota

**Claim.** Participants can create a limited set of VPC resources in a shared VPC, such as network interfaces and security groups, and those resources count against the participant account's VPC quotas, not the owner's.

**Write it as.** `create a limited set of VPC resources` · `VPC quotas in the participant account`

**Scope.** participants in a shared VPC.

> "Participants can create a limited set of VPC resources in a shared VPC. For example, participants can create network interfaces and security groups, and enable VPC flow logs for the network interfaces that they own. The VPC resources that a participant creates count against the VPC quotas in the participant account, not the owner account."
> — [Responsibilities and permissions for owners and participants](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-share-limitations.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### ram-vpc-participants-no-route-tables-nat

**Claim.** In a shared VPC subnet, participants cannot work with route tables (they can only describe them) and cannot create, delete or describe NAT gateways.

**Write it as.** `Participants cannot work with route tables` · `Participants cannot create, delete, or describe NAT gateways`

**Scope.** participants in a shared VPC subnet.

> "Participants cannot work with route tables (for example, create, delete, or associate route tables) in a shared VPC subnet. Participants can describe route tables in a shared VPC subnet."
> — [Responsibilities and permissions for owners and participants](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-share-limitations.html)

> "Participants cannot create, delete, or describe NAT gateways in a shared VPC subnet."
> — [Responsibilities and permissions for owners and participants](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-share-limitations.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### ram-vs-resource-policy-org-ou-without-ids

**Claim.** Compared with sharing through a resource-based policy, RAM can share with an organization or OU without listing every account ID, and shared resources appear in the consumer's service console and APIs; resources shared by a resource-based policy are not visible this way and must be referenced by ARN.

**Write it as.** `enumerate every one of the AWS account IDs` · `resources were directly in the user's account` · `shared by attaching a resource-based policy aren't visible`

**Scope.** AWS RAM compared with resource-based policies.

> "You can share with an organization or an organizational unit (OU) without having to enumerate every one of the AWS account IDs."
> — [What is AWS Resource Access Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/what-is.html)

> "Users can see the resources shared with them directly in the originating AWS service console and API operations as if those resources were directly in the user's account."
> — [What is AWS Resource Access Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/what-is.html)

> "Resources shared by attaching a resource-based policy aren't visible this way; instead, you have to discover and explicitly refer to the resource by its Amazon Resource Name (ARN)."
> — [What is AWS Resource Access Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/what-is.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### ram-whole-organization-counts-as-one-principal

**Scope.** per resource share; sharing with the organization ID.

> "Each shared principal that you reference in a resource share adds one to your quota use. If you share with an entire organization by referencing its ID, it counts as only one against this quota."
> — [Service quotas for AWS RAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/service-quotas.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.
